Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI comparisons of GM between substance users and controls), I2 (no specific grey-matter structural measures reported), I3 (no empirical substance-specific data provided).

Excluded under E3: the primary grouping variable is psychotic diagnosis (psychosis vs controls) with cannabis use as a subgroup, not substance-use vs control. Inclusion met: I1 (empirical MRI GM study) and I2 (GM density measure). Inclusion not demonstrated: none of the listed inclusion criteria are clearly unmet, but substance-users are not compared as a primary grouping independent of a psychiatric patient group, so E3 applies.

Empirical VBM MRI study (Frontiers in Psychiatry, English) comparing gray-matter volume between 25 betel-quid chewers and 25 controls, reporting GMV differences and associations with dependence. Meets inclusion: I1 (MRI VBM study, users vs controls), I2 (GM volume measure), I3 (substance of abuse: betel quid). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract coordinates and further details.

The study examines internet gaming disorder (a behavioral/psychiatric patient group), not substance users; therefore exclusion criterion E3 applies. The study did assess gray matter volume (I2 met). It does not meet I1 (not an MRI comparison of substance users vs controls) and I3 (not about substance use).

The study is an empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volumes across cocaine-use disorder and healthy controls (and gambling disorder). It reports GMV differences involving cocaine users, meeting the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

The study compares hepatitis C (HCV) patients to healthy controls — a medical patient group — and does not investigate substance users. Inclusion met: I2 (surface-based cortical thickness measure). Inclusion not met: I1 (not a substance-user vs control MRI study) and I3 (no substance examined). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are clearly met based on the abstract.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses cortical thickness GM measure), I3 (addresses alcohol, an in-scope substance). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 — the study does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls; it is a prospective cohort predicting later binge drinking rather than a comparison of users vs controls. Therefore EXCLUDE.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing cannabis users and non-users, reporting grey-matter structural measures (GM volume/density and cortical thickness). No exclusion criteria are met (not a pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review). Include for full-text review.

Exclusion E3: study groups are schizophrenia patients (with/without substance use) versus healthy controls — psychiatric patient grouping, not substance-use grouping. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (empirical MRI VBM comparing substance-using patients to controls), I2 (GM volume measure), I3 (substances include cannabis/alcohol). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: none additional. Therefore exclude based on E3.

Empirical English-language T1 MRI study reporting gray matter volume changes in treatment-seeking cocaine users with a healthy control group. Uses GM volume measures and involves a substance of abuse (cocaine). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group non-substance comparison, or review). Include for full-text review to extract user-vs-control structural data and coordinates if available.

Study is not an empirical MRI comparison of substance users vs controls and concerns behavioral (internet/gaming) addiction rather than substance use. exclusion IDs met: []; inclusion IDs met: I2 (mentions GM volume/density); inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (participants are gamers/internet users, not substance users).

Empirical English MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients (n=19) and healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry measures of gray-matter asymmetry. Fits inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract regional GM alterations.

This article is a narrative review/overview of OUD neurobiology, not an empirical MRI study, therefore it meets exclusion E4. Inclusion criteria are not demonstrated: I1 (empirical GM comparisons) not met; I2 and I3 not demonstrated with primary data.

E4 applies: the article is a neuroimaging meta-analysis (not an original empirical MRI study). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls), I2 and I3 not applicable/not demonstrated. Therefore excluded based on E4.

Excluded due to E1: the study used a pharmacological manipulation (varenicline) during the smoking cessation treatment. Inclusion criteria met: I1 (empirical English MRI VBM study comparing smokers and non-smokers), I2 (GM volume measure), I3 (substance = nicotine). No inclusion criteria are unmet or not demonstrated from the abstract.

Exclusion E4 met: this is a review/overview article rather than an original empirical study. Inclusion criteria met: none (no empirical MRI comparison reported). Inclusion criteria not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I2 (no specific grey-matter structural measures reported as original data), I3 (substance-specific empirical data not presented). Full text review not required based on abstract.

Prospective sMRI study comparing heavy cannabis users (N=20) to controls (N=22) with GM volume estimated (VBM); meets inclusion criteria for MRI Grey Matter comparisons in substance users. No exclusion criteria met (not pharmacological, not lesion, not patient-group-based, not a review). Include for full-text review to extract region-specific effects.

Abstract does not report any comparisons between substance users and controls, so inclusion criterion I1 (empirical MRI study of GM differences between substance users and controls) is not met. The study does report striatal and cortical volumes (I2 met). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are evident. Inclusion criterion I3 (any substance) is not demonstrated/applicable. Therefore exclude from the review.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent subjects to healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry to assess regional grey matter volume, meeting I1 and I2; substance is alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group-other-than-substance, or review). Include for full-text review.

Abstract provides insufficient information to confirm it is an empirical MRI study comparing medication-overuse (a form of substance use) patients with an appropriate control group. Title implies gray-matter changes related to medication overuse in chronic migraine, but methods, imaging modality, substance type, and comparison groups are not reported. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to assess I1–I3.

EXCLUDED: Study examines Internet addiction (behavioral), not substance use. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E4 not applicable). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses grey-matter structural measure: GMD via VBM). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a study of substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of a substance of abuse). Does not meet core requirement of substance-user sample.

Abstract reports cortical thickness MRI analyses in adolescent methamphetamine users (cortical thickness qualifies per I2; substance is methamphetamine, qualifies per I3). The abstract does not clearly state comparisons with healthy controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether GM differences vs controls were assessed.

Study examines social networking site (technology) addiction, not substance use; therefore it does not meet I1 (MRI studies comparing substance users vs controls) or I3 (studies of substances of abuse). It does meet I2 (uses voxel-based morphometry/GM volume). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met.

Excluded because this article is a meta-analysis (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (addresses grey-matter measures via voxel-based morphometry) and I3 (studies substances: cocaine and methamphetamine). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between heavy- and light-drinking adolescents (alcohol users vs controls). This meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (alcohol is an eligible substance). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated. Include for full-text review to confirm methodological details.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing cannabis users (n=141) and controls (n=120) reporting cortical surface measures (cortical thickness, surface area, gyrification). Matches inclusion criteria for GM structural measures and substance use comparisons; no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

E4: This is a voxelwise meta-analysis (systematic review/meta-analysis) and thus excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (addresses grey-matter VBM measures) and I3 (studies nicotine/cigarette smokers). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study assessing GM differences; it's a meta-analysis).

Exclusion E3: study compares gambling disorder (a psychiatric/behavioral addiction) patients to healthy controls rather than substance users, so it does not meet I1 (substance-user sample). Inclusion I2 is met (cortical thickness MRI measure). No other exclusion criteria apparent. I1 not demonstrated; I3 (any substance) not applicable/not demonstrated.

Study compares substance-naïve offspring with a family history of alcoholism versus controls, not substance users. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E4 not applicable). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (surface-based cortical thickness MRI). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls), I3 not applicable because participants are substance-naïve. Therefore excluded from this substance-user vs control meta-analysis.

Abstract reports MRI findings in methcathinone (substance) abusers but does not clearly state comparison of grey-matter volume/density or specific GM structural measures versus controls. I3 (any substance) is met. I1 and I2 are not demonstrated from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether GM volume/density comparisons with controls were performed and which structural measures were used.

Abstract reports an empirical structural neuroimaging study relating alcohol and cannabis use to gray matter (GM) volume and white matter integrity in adolescents and adults. It assesses GM volume measures and compares substance use to controls. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI study assessing grey-matter structural differences (cortical thickness and cortical volume) between amphetamine-type stimulant users and drug-naïve controls, matching the review objective. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are apparent from the abstract.

Abstract reports a methodological study applying cortical thickness to associations with drinking in 148 at-risk males. Inclusion criteria I2 (cortical thickness measure) and I3 (alcohol as substance) are met. I1 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) is not demonstrated — no case-control comparison is reported. No exclusion criteria appear to be met. Abstract lacks sufficient information to determine if group comparisons were performed; full-text review needed.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses GM volume measures). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a substance-user vs control MRI study), I3 (does not involve substance of abuse; studies online game addiction, a behavioral addiction).

Empirical VBM MRI study comparing abstinent heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls, reporting gray matter density reductions (right DLPFC) and associations with duration of heroin use. Meets inclusion: I1 (MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I2 (uses GM density structural measure), I3 (substance = opioids/heroin). No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing abstinent alcoholics with controls using surface-based cortical thickness to map grey-matter loss; meets I1 (MRI GM comparison), I2 (cortical thickness allowed), and I3 (alcohol is an eligible substance). No exclusion criteria evident. Include for full-text review.

Study examines grey-matter surface-based measures (surface area) related to alcohol and cannabis initiation in adolescents, addressing the review objective. No exclusion criteria are identified. The abstract implies imaging (surface measures) but does not explicitly state MRI or control-group comparisons; full text needed to confirm methods and comparisons.

Study examines internet (behavioral) addiction rather than substance use; thus does not meet requirement to assess substance users vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cortical thickness is a gray-matter structural measure). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a substance-use sample), I3 (not a study of any psychoactive substance). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met.

No exclusion criteria are met. Abstract reports resting-state fMRI with VBM gray-matter volume examined as a covariate, but does not clearly report case-control GM volume differences required by I1. Substance (betel quid) is within scope (I3). Insufficient information to confirm I1/I2, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an empirical VBM MRI study comparing opiate-dependent subjects to controls and reporting gray-matter density decreases. This meets inclusion criteria for MRI assessment of GM differences (I1), accepts GM density as a qualifying measure (I2), and the substance (opioids/opiate dependence) is within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey-matter (subcortical volume) between alcohol-dependent, polysubstance users and healthy controls. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apparent from abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

EXCLUDED because this article is a meta-analysis (E4). It analyzes GM differences in alcohol-use disorder, so it meets I2 (grey-matter structural measures) and I3 (substance = alcohol). It does not meet I1 (not an original empirical MRI study).

This empirical MRI study compares children with prenatal alcohol exposure (ARND) to controls and examines cortical thickness and surface area (surface-based grey-matter measures). It therefore meets I1 (empirical MRI comparison with controls), I2 (uses cortical thickness/SA as GM measures), and I3 (alcohol as the substance). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Study compares gambling disorder (behavioral addiction) patients to controls, not substance users. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (psychiatric patient group as grouping variable). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (voxel-based morphometry assessing GM volume). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user sample), I3 (not about substance abuse).

Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter volume between heroin users and controls (n=78 vs 79), so it meets I1 and I2. Substance is heroin (an opioid), meeting I3. No exclusion criteria are evident (no pharmacological manipulation, no brain lesion study, not a psychiatric patient-group comparison, not a review). Full text review recommended to extract specific regional data and methods.

The study compares baseline grey matter volumes between occasional stimulant users who escalated use versus those who maintained/reduced use — it does not compare substance users to non-user controls, so I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses GM volume measures), I3 (studies stimulants). No exclusion criteria are met (E1-E4 not applicable). Thus excluded for failing to meet I1 (no user vs control comparison).

Empirical MRI morphometric study in English comparing chronic alcohol users to nonalcoholic controls and reporting regional brain (grey-matter) volumes. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion focus, or patient-group other than substance use; not a review. Full-text needed to extract data and confirm details.

Title and abstract indicate an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study of gray matter abnormalities in betel-quid-dependent patients compared to controls. Betel quid is an eligible substance. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison, or review) are met based on the abstract.

Exclusion E3 met: study compares a psychiatric patient group (clinically depressed adolescents) to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (voxel-based morphometry assessing GM volume). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user vs control study), I3 (no substance of abuse studied).

Longitudinal empirical MRI morphometry comparing heavy-drinking adolescents to nondrinkers; assesses regional brain structural differences (fits grey-matter structural measures) and involves alcohol as the substance. No exclusion criteria met from abstract. Full text needed to confirm exact GM metric and details.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing alcohol-dependent individuals to age-matched healthy controls reporting gray matter volume differences related to decision-making. No exclusion criteria met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric grouping as primary variable, or review). Full-text review appropriate to extract coordinates and methods.

Study does not compare substance users to controls and so does not meet I1. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses voxel-based morphometry/GM structural measure). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user vs control comparison), I3 (not about substances).

Excluded: animal experimental study with in utero alcohol administration (E1). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cortical thickness measured) and I3 (alcohol as substance). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls; mouse embryonic histology rather than human MRI).

Excluded because population is behavioral (mobile phone) addiction, not substance users: inclusion I1 (MRI of substance users vs controls) is not met. Inclusion met: I2 (grey-matter structural measure assessed: GMV). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not substance use sample), I3 (not a study of any substance). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract reports empirical MRI study using cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) comparing chronic cocaine users and controls; addresses GM structural differences between substance users (stimulant) and controls, meeting inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria met. Sufficient info for inclusion for full-text review to extract data on cortical thickness and group comparisons.

No exclusion criteria met. Study is a VBM investigation of time perspective in (presumably) healthy subjects, not a comparison of substance users vs controls; thus I1 (MRI study comparing substance users and controls) is not met. I2 (uses grey-matter volume via VBM) is met. I3 (study of substance use) is not met.

Empirical English MRI study comparing heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls using cortical thickness (a valid surface-based GM measure). Substance = opioids (heroin). No exclusion criteria met from abstract (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group other than substance users, or review).

Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing current smokers to never-smokers and reporting gray matter volume differences attributable to nicotine; meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Abstract reports cortical morphometry in substance-dependent individuals (a grey-matter structural measure) and is about substance dependence, but it does not explicitly state comparison with controls or explicitly name MRI; include for full-text to confirm I1.

Empirical English MRI study comparing adolescent substance users (SUD) to matched controls using T1 structural images and cortical thickness analyses. This satisfies I1 (MRI GM comparison), I2 (surface-based cortical thickness measure), and I3 (substance use sample). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, no lesion study, not a psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison, not a review). Recommend full-text review to extract drug class details and methods.

No user-vs-control GM comparison reported: study reports VBM measures within 49 cocaine users only and relates GMV to TMS responses. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (VBM GM volume measures), I3 (substance: cocaine). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (no comparison between substance users and controls).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing structural (grey matter) measures in nicotine-dependent smokers vs controls using SUIT; fits the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Excluded: this is a review article (E4). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study), I2 (no original grey-matter structural measures reported), I3 (addresses substances but only in narrative review form, not as empirical data).

Empirical MRI study comparing cortical thickness and volume between marijuana users and controls in emerging adults. Meets I1 (MRI study assessing GM differences), I2 (surface-based measure: cortical thickness/volume), and I3 (cannabis as substance). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Excluded because grouping variable is behavioral (online gaming addiction), not substance use — exclusion E3 applies. Inclusion I2 is satisfied (structural MRI cortical thickness). Inclusion I1 (empirical MRI of substance users vs controls) is not met; I3 (any substance) not met/not applicable.

Title/abstract report gray matter changes linked to methamphetamine (meets I2 and I3). Abstract does not explicitly state use of MRI methods or comparison between substance users and controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Given insufficient detail to confirm all inclusion criteria, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals comparing brain gray matter to controls, reporting prefrontal GM reductions. This addresses structural GM differences in a substance-using sample (stimulant), meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract examines prefrontal cortical thickness in betel-quid-dependent chewers (a grey-matter surface measure) and betel quid is an in-scope substance. However the abstract does not clearly state MRI methods or that users were compared to control subjects (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm group comparison and MRI details.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter density between methamphetamine users and healthy controls (stimulant class). GM density is an eligible structural measure. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or patient-group diagnosis as primary grouping is reported. Meets inclusion criteria for full-text review.

Empirical MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent (recovering) participants to light-drinking controls using deformation-based morphometry to assess tissue (including grey matter) volume differences and longitudinal changes; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes longitudinal prediction of future substance use in psychiatrically unwell youth using neural activity/structure, not a cross-sectional MRI comparison of substance users versus controls. Therefore I1 is not met; I2 and I3 are not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are clearly met.

Study examines alcohol misuse and mood disorders following traumatic brain injury (a neurological brain-lesion patient group) and does not report MRI grey-matter structural comparisons between substance users and controls. Exclusion met: E2 (brain lesion/TBI), E3 (neurological patient group). Inclusion met: I3 (study involves alcohol). Inclusion not met: I1 and I2 (no evidence of empirical MRI GM measures reported).

Abstract reports cortical gray matter loss in treatment-naïve alcohol-dependent individuals versus controls, addressing GM structural differences relevant to the review. The abstract does not explicitly state MRI modality, so full text is needed to confirm imaging methods and GM measure details.

Empirical MRI study comparing gray-matter volume between methamphetamine users and controls, meeting inclusion criteria for language and MRI GM volume measures (I1,I2) and substance type (I3). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison unrelated to substance use, or review). Include for full-text review to extract regional GM differences.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine users to non-drug controls and reports grey-matter structural measures (cortical volumes/thickness and nucleus accumbens volume). It addresses a substance of abuse (methamphetamine, a stimulant). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are met.
Study reports MRI structural differences (reduced dorsal prefrontal gray matter) in chronic ketamine users versus controls, satisfying inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder patients to controls and reporting grey-matter density reductions. Meets I1 (MRI GM differences vs controls), I2 (GM density measure), and I3 (alcohol). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing grey matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and THC-naive controls, meeting I1 (MRI GM differences) and I2 (GM volume measure). Substance is cannabis, within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria appear met: no pharmacological manipulation, no lesion study, not a psychiatric patient-group comparison, and not a review. Include for full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing binge drinkers (substance users) to healthy controls and reporting grey-matter volumetric correlates. Meets inclusion criteria for GM volume measures and substance (alcohol). No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Study used task-based functional MRI of reward processing, not structural GM measures. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (contains alcohol-dependent group). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences vs controls) and I2 (no grey-matter structural measure such as GM volume/density/thickness reported).

Excluded because this is an integrative review (E4). No original empirical MRI comparison of substance users vs controls is reported: inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3 are not met or not demonstrated. The paper reviews structural/functional imaging in gambling disorder (a behavioral addiction), not empirical GM volume studies of substance-using groups vs controls.

The study reports MRI-based gray matter volume reductions in synthetic cannabinoid users versus healthy controls, meeting inclusion criteria I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (substance of abuse: synthetic cannabinoids). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met; include for full-text review.

E3: This study compares a neurological patient group (chronic migraine) to controls rather than substance users. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI of substance users vs controls absent), I3 (not a substance-using sample), I2 (grey-matter measure of substance use not applicable).

Abstract reports an empirical structural MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volume in male adolescents with substance and conduct problems to controls, satisfying I1 and I2; substances are within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry reporting regional gray matter concentration reductions in MDMA (polydrug) users versus non-users. Matches inclusion criteria: MRI GM comparison (I1), GM concentration measure (I2), substance study (MDMA) within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are met in the abstract.

Study compares dependent vs non-dependent anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) users rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (investigates a substance of abuse: AAS). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no clear MRI comparison of substance users vs non-user controls), I2 (abstract does not explicitly report grey-matter structural measures).

The study examines bone microarchitecture in hepatic cirrhosis, not brain MRI or grey-matter differences between substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an MRI grey-matter study), I2 (does not assess grey-matter structural measures), I3 (not a substance-use study). Therefore excluded from this review.

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing gray matter volume in substance-dependent individuals versus controls, finding reduced medial OFC GM. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing FASD (prenatal alcohol exposure) participants to matched controls using cortical thickness (a valid grey-matter structural measure). Addresses alcohol-related GM structural differences and no exclusion criteria are met.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent men and healthy controls; reports regional GM volume decreases and correlations with executive performance. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract regional GM alterations.

Large pooled MRI mega-analysis comparing gray matter volumes in substance-dependent individuals vs controls across multiple drug classes, matching the review objective. No indication of pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-grouping as primary variable, or being a review/meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not compare substance users with controls: inclusion I1 not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness and subcortical GM volume measures). No exclusion criteria were met (none).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study concerns amphetamine abuse, an in-scope substance). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original empirical MRI study assessing GM differences; it is a narrative review), I2 (does not report original grey-matter measures). Therefore exclude for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because E4: this is a systematic literature review, not an original empirical MRI study. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (empirical English-language MRI study comparing substance users and controls) is not met; I2 (grey-matter structural measure) not applicable as primary data are not reported; I3 (study of substance users) is not met—focus is Internet Gaming Disorder (behavioral addiction), not substance use.

E4 met: this publication is a systematic review (not original empirical research). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM comparisons), I2 (does not present original grey-matter structural measures), I3 (although cannabis is the topic, primary empirical substance-user GM data are not reported in this review). Therefore exclude as a review article.

Empirical MRI study (English) reporting grey-matter volume (cingulum) differences associated with cannabis use (users vs non-users). Satisfies I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria clearly met from the abstract; grouping is cannabis use rather than psychiatric diagnosis. Include for full-text to verify sample/contrast details and extract data if eligible.

Excluded (E3): study compares adolescents with conduct disorder (a psychiatric patient group) vs controls — grouping is psychiatric diagnosis, not substance use. Inclusion: I2 met (reports cortical thickness/surface-based grey-matter measures). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 not met (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 not demonstrated (not about substance use).

Study compares alcohol‑naïve genetically vulnerable rats to controls rather than substance users versus controls; therefore I1 (comparison of substance users and controls) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (VBM grey-matter measure), I3 (substance = alcohol). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1–E4 not applicable).

Abstract reports empirical MRI study comparing cortical thickness/volume between substance users (methamphetamine-dependent) and controls, assessing grey-matter structural measures and interaction with HIV; meets inclusion criteria I1 and I2. No exclusion criteria met. Some uncertainty about primary focus on HIV but substance dependence is a grouping variable, so include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to determine if it compares cannabis users vs controls (I1 not demonstrated). Title/abstract indicate MRI cortical thickness (thinner entorhinal cortex) and focus on cannabis liability, satisfying I2 and I3. No exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review to confirm group comparison and measures.

Excluded: study compares schizophrenia patients to controls (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls), I2 (no substance-related GM measures), I3 (not a substance-using sample).

Study compares adolescents with family history of AUD (FH+ vs FH-), not substance users versus controls; therefore it does not meet I1. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness, a permitted GM measure) and I3 (alcohol is the relevant substance). Inclusion not met: I1 (no MRI comparison of substance users and controls). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) appear to apply.

Empirical MRI study comparing grey matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid users and healthy controls, reporting reduced total and regional GM volume; meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (substance of abuse). No exclusion criteria appear to apply (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review).

Title and abstract address cortical gray matter loss in methamphetamine users versus controls, suggesting relevant GM structural differences (I2) for a substance in scope (I3). The abstract does not explicitly confirm MRI methods or specific GM measure details (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met; full-text review needed to confirm methods and measures.

Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no original empirical MRI study comparing substance users to controls), I2 (no primary report of its own grey-matter structural measures), I3 (unclear/other medication-overuse population not presented as substance-user cohort).

E4 met: Abstract describes an evaluation/review of female enrollment and methods across structural neuroimaging studies rather than reporting original empirical MRI comparisons. Inclusion criteria I1-I3 are not demonstrated: no primary empirical GM volume/thickness comparisons between substance users and controls are reported.
